title: Lisse Hom descent from affine coefficient-section restriction
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme and $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, and put $\Lambda_Z=p_Z^*\Lambda$ on the small pro-etale site of every scheme $Z$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their restriction to slice sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Assume that for every affine object $W\to X$ of this site, writing $W_V=W\times_XV$, actual coefficient restriction
$$\Gamma(W,\Lambda_X)\longrightarrow\Gamma(W_V,\Lambda_V)$$
is bijective. Let $M,N$ be lisse $\Lambda_X$-modules, meaning pro-etale locally finite free, with ranks allowed to vary [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Then actual restriction is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_X}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_V}(j^*M,j^*N).$$
For any common affine pro-etale trivializing cover $\{W_i\to X\}$ with $M|_{W_i}\cong\Lambda_{W_i}^{a_i}$ and $N|_{W_i}\cong\Lambda_{W_i}^{b_i}$, the inverse is characterized by entrywise inverse coefficient restriction on the $b_i\times a_i$ matrix of a morphism. It is independent of the cover and bases, and these local maps agree on all overlap refinements and glue uniquely. Rank zero and the empty scheme are allowed. Moreover, let $f:X'\to X$ be a scheme morphism, set $V'=X'\times_XV$, with open immersion $j':V'\hookrightarrow X'$ and projection $g:V'\to V$, and assume the same coefficient-section bijection on every affine pro-etale object over $X'$. Let $f^*$, $g^*$, $j'^*$ denote the module pullbacks with their composition isomorphisms [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Whenever $f^*M,f^*N$ are lisse, the Hom bijections commute with pullback under the canonical coefficient identifications: for a morphism $u:j^*M\to j^*N$, with $e$ and $e'$ the respective inverse restriction maps, one has
$$f^*e(u)=e'(g^*u)$$
after the canonical comparisons $j'^*f^*\cong g^*j^*$. This assertion concerns morphisms between given lisse modules, not extension of objects from $V$.

proof.text: Use the internal/sectionwise equivalence to regard the modules as module sheaves; it preserves sections and restriction maps identically. The coefficient-localization lemma identifies the site over every pro-etale object $W$ with the slice and identifies $\Lambda_X(W)$ with $\Gamma(W,\Lambda_W)$, compatibly with actual restriction. In particular it applies to $V$ and $W_V$. Module pullback along such an object is slice restriction: in the defining formula $\Lambda_W\otimes_{u^{-1}\Lambda_X}u^{-1}M$, inverse image is restriction and the coefficient map is the specified isomorphism, so $b\otimes m\mapsto\alpha_u^{-1}(b)m$ gives the identification. Thus all subsequent restrictions are the actual maps in the statement.

proof.text: Choose trivializing covers for $M$ and $N$ from the lisse definition. Pull one cover back to each member of the other and compose the covers, using the site axioms; both modules are free on the resulting common cover $\{C_k\to X\}$. Replace it by the family of all affine open subschemes of all $C_k$. Affine opens form a basis. Source locality of weak etaleness ensures these restrictions remain site objects. For each affine open $U\subset X$, the covering condition for $\{C_k\to X\}$ already supplies finitely many affine opens $A_j\subset C_{k_j}$ whose images cover $U$; each $A_j$ itself is a member of the new family, so these same witnesses prove its covering condition. Thus there is a common affine trivializing cover $\{W_i\to X\}$ with finite ranks $a_i,b_i$. For an overlap scheme $P$, its family of all affine opens is likewise a cover: each affine open of $P$ itself supplies a single witness to the finite-affine condition. No assertion that $P$ is affine, and no separation hypothesis, is used.

proof.text: On any affine object $T\to X$ on which both modules have chosen free bases, the free-matrix lemma identifies morphisms with $b\times a$ matrices over $\Gamma(T,\Lambda_T)$. Apply it also on the slice over $T_V$, which need not be affine. The displayed section formula in that lemma, and the coefficient-localization compatibility, show that restricting a morphism restricts each matrix entry by the actual coefficient-section map $r_T$. Thus restriction on these Hom sets is bijective: its inverse replaces every entry $c$ by the unique $r_T^{-1}(c)$. This uses exactly the hypothesis on the affine object $T$, not a hypothesis that $T_V$ is affine. In particular it gives injectivity for any two maps expressed in any fixed bases on $T$.

proof.text: Given $u:j^*M\to j^*N$, extend its matrix on every $(W_i)_V$ by Step 3, obtaining $e_i:M|_{W_i}\to N|_{W_i}$. Put $P=W_i\times_XW_j$. On every affine open $T$ in an affine cover of $P$, the restrictions of both $e_i$ and $e_j$ are maps between the same two free modules. Express both in the bases inherited from $W_i$. Their restrictions to $T_V$ are both the restriction of $u$, regardless of the bases originally used to construct $e_j$. Injectivity from Step 3 gives equality on $T$. The Hom-sheaf separatedness gives equality on $P$. The Hom-sheaf gluing property on $\{W_i\to X\}$ now gives a unique global map $e(u)$ restricting to $e_i$. Its restriction to $V$ equals $u$, since they agree on the covering $\{(W_i)_V\to V\}$.

proof.text: If $h,k:M\to N$ have equal restrictions to $V$, Step 3 gives $h|_{W_i}=k|_{W_i}$ for every $i$. Separatedness of the Hom sheaf gives $h=k$. Together with Step 4 this proves the claimed bijection. Any other cover or bases produce an extension with the same restriction, so injectivity identifies it with $e(u)$. On any affine overlap refinement Step 3 likewise identifies the two local maps, and equality persists under all further restrictions. This proves the asserted characterization, independence and agreement on refinements without a comparison formula for transition matrices.

For the Cartesian square in the statement apply Steps 1--5 on $X'$; their assumptions are exactly the stipulated coefficient bijections and lisseness of $f^*M,f^*N$. Let $c_M:j'^*f^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*j^*M$ and $c_N$ be the comparisons obtained from the module composition isomorphisms and $f\circ j'=j\circ g$. Naturality gives $c_N\circ j'^*(f^*e(u))=g^*(j^*e(u))\circ c_M=g^*u\circ c_M$. By definition $e'(g^*u)$ has precisely this restriction, with the same comparisons. The injectivity already proved on $X'$ therefore gives $f^*e(u)=e'(g^*u)$. This verifies the actual comparison square, rather than claiming entrywise compatibility for a pullback chart which might not be affine.

proof.text: If either local rank is zero, the free-matrix lemma gives a singleton Hom set and the entrywise inverse is the unique empty matrix. For the empty scheme the empty covering and the Hom sheaf axiom give a singleton set of global morphisms. All gluing and uniqueness arguments above therefore include these cases. For the identity open every $r_T$ is the identity, so the constructed inverse is the identity.

The claim is true: Hom(M,|U,N|U) and Hom over the slice at U_V are sheaves, and restriction between them is entrywise r_T on every affine object T where M and N are free; such T cover everything. Step 1 identifies j^* with slice restriction via α_j (coefficient-sections-localization). Step 2 refines the composed cover to all affine opens using the original fpqc witnesses, with no affine-overlap claim (E1 checked). Step 3 applies the matrix lemma on the slices at T and T_V, which need only final objects. Step 4 compares e_i and e_j in one basis on affine T ⊂ P, then uses Hom-sheaf separatedness and gluing. Step 5 gives injectivity and independence of cover and bases. Step 6 proves base change from naturality of the composition isomorphisms plus injectivity on X'. Step 7 covers the edge cases. I also tested V=∅, which forces Λ_X=0 so the claim holds, and V=X, rank 0, X=∅ and Λ=0. The citer root-tower step 4 supplies the extra base-change hypotheses. The rg -L duplicate search found only different results: lisse-morphism-rigidity and normalized-open-refinement-coherence.
